title: GitHub's AI Powered Security Platform: Sarah Khalife
talk_summary: A GitHub solutions engineer demos GitHub Advanced Security (code scanning/CodeQL, secret scanning, Dependabot) and its new AI features: code-scanning autofix, AI-generated custom secret regexes, and AI triage of unstructured passwords. The transferable core is using a deterministic analyzer's data-flow context to ground an LLM fix suggestion inside the PR, plus coverage/alert dashboards to find what scanning misses.

takeaways.technique: Analyzer-grounded autofix suggestions in the PR
takeaways.what_they_do: CodeQL computes the source-to-sink data flow and common fix patterns, and that structured context is fed into the LLM prompt so the suggested fix is specific to the actual vulnerability path rather than generic.
takeaways.numbers: auto fix successful for ~70% of customer use cases (public beta)

takeaways.what_they_do: The suggested fix is committed inside the pull request and all scans rerun immediately, so remediation is verified before merge rather than after.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as soon as I commit that fix, it will rerun all the scans so we can see if that vulnerability is actually remediated right off the bat

takeaways.what_they_do: Blocks pushes containing detected secrets before they enter git history, so revocation isn't needed; also scans history, PRs and comments for already-leaked secrets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it allows you to block any pushes that are coming to the GitHub ecosystem before the secret is being exposed

takeaways.what_they_do: Users supply sample strings and the LLM drafts the regex/custom pattern as a starting point, replacing manual regex authoring.

takeaways.technique: Coverage view to find unscanned surface
takeaways.what_they_do: An org-level dashboard shows what fraction of repos are actually covered by each scanner, exposing repos that never run through CI and thus are never scanned.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're not actually getting coverage unless you're going through a CI pipeline. But, there's so many more repositories that probably are just sitting there
takeaways.numbers: example org: secret scanning 99% coverage, code scanning 57%

takeaways.technique: AI triage to suppress false positives
takeaways.what_they_do: For noisy unstructured detections (e.g., 'password =' strings), an LLM analyzes repository context to judge whether it's a true positive, labeling uncertain ones separately rather than alerting blindly.
